In the attendee list, the organisation sees your name, the number of tickets and whether they have been used – never your email address or payment data; other guests only see numbers. If you report after an event that it did not take place, we store the report with your optional note so that the Pickeed team can review it before the payout. For organisations, we store the identifier of the Stripe account and its status; Stripe collects and checks identity, company and bank account. We keep order and payment details as long as accounting and possible disputes require (usually 10 years); if you delete your account, only «Deleted account» is shown there.

If our email service Brevo reports that an email could not be delivered (e.g. invalid address, mailbox does not exist, delivery blocked) or that someone marked an email from Pickeed as spam, Brevo sends us this report automatically (webhook). We then store only a check value of the email address (never the address itself), the reason and the times. We no longer send reminders and notices to blocked addresses (e.g. meeting reminders, the waiting list, trusted people, guests, open calls); we still try to send sign-in codes. For temporary errors (e.g. a full mailbox), we only block an address after three reports within 30 days; such entries without a block are deleted after 30 days without a new report. The report identifiers we use to recognise duplicate reports are deleted after 30 days. We lift a block as soon as you sign in with a code or confirm in your profile that your address works again; otherwise the check value remains – even after an account is deleted, so that we no longer send emails to an address that does not receive them or has reported spam. Your profile shows a notice if emails to your address are not arriving.

When you visit the website, our server processes technically necessary details such as IP address, time and requested address in order to deliver the page and prevent abuse. We keep these server logs (including IP address) for at most 30 days and then delete them automatically. We do not track you and use no analytics or advertising services. To run the service, we store on which days an account was active (no content, only for overall figures and support) and delete this after 400 days or together with the account.

We process data to provide Pickeed to you (contract), to run the service securely and prevent abuse (legitimate interest), and for optional features such as calendar or notifications (your consent, which you can withdraw at any time). We show public creator pages and public events because you publish them (contract). Suggestions of offers are based only on a plan's details (occasion, theme, place, group size, budget) and on the members' preferences and dietary needs – combined and without names –, never on your messages. Whether an offer may appear as «Sponsored» depends only on the plan's details. We only process sensitive data (diet, allergies and accessibility in a plan, and emergency info) with your explicit consent. In company spaces we process data on the company's behalf (data processing on behalf, terms section 6b); there, the company is responsible for the processing.

We set a technically necessary session cookie for signing in (also for guests without an account) and – only if you arrive via a referral link – a cookie with its code until you sign up (at most 60 days). We also set: a short session tag («pk_s», only 8 characters of a check value, readable by the app so that it does not show old data after switching accounts), two short-lived cookies when you sign in with Google or Apple (at most 10 and 30 minutes), a cookie with the code of a founder invitation if you come via such a link (at most 60 days), and – only if an age under 16 was entered when signing up – the cookie «pk_ak» with a random device ID for 30 days, so that no new sign-up with a different date is possible during that time (see «Date of birth and age checks»). In your browser we also remember your language and which area (private, company, provider) you opened last, and store website files for offline use. There are no advertising or tracking cookies.

Several accounts on one device (E-107): if you sign in with another account, the previous one stays signed in on this device – a second, technically necessary cookie stores only the sessions of these accounts (at most five), never passwords or email addresses. Every request always applies only to the account that is currently active. Companies and creators can have their own account with their own email address; we confirm a company or business email with a code (check value, valid for 10 minutes). If you move private plans or memories to another account of yours, we log what was moved for 30 days so you can undo it.

Acting as a business or creator: if you are the owner or an admin of a business or a creator page belongs to you, you can act as that account in the business or creator area – for example write and react in the account’s one-to-one chat, give hearts and comments, follow, save posts, block people, create offers and handle creator bookings. Others then see the account’s name and picture, not yours. For messages in the account’s chat we store which person wrote them; only people who also act for the account can see this. We check consent to the terms and age for you as a person. If your account is paused, you cannot act as a business or creator.
5. Where data is stored – service providers
, Geneva, Switzerland – server on which Pickeed runs.

, USA – operation of the database. The database is located in the data centre in Zurich (Switzerland). Supabase is a US company; access from the USA is only intended for support and operations, but cannot be ruled out. For this we rely on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses with the adaptations required for Switzerland, which are part of Supabase's data processing agreement.

(Sendinblue SAS, Paris, France) – sending sign-in codes and notices by email. For this, Brevo receives your email address and the content of the email. Brevo does not store the content of our emails; delivery logs are deleted after one month; opens are counted anonymously at most. Brevo reports delivery failures and spam complaints back to us (see «Emails that don't arrive»).

, Dublin, Ireland – for the provider plan (and company and event subscriptions taken out earlier): card payment, invoices and cancellation. Stripe receives the name of the company, business profile or person, the email address of the person taking out the subscription and the card details; Pickeed never sees card details. Stripe is partly responsible for payment processing itself and may process data in the USA (standard contractual clauses).

(Stripe Payments Europe Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) – ticket sales for public events as well as paid creator bookings and meetups and experiences: Stripe processes payments with TWINT and card, sends them directly to the organisation's Stripe account, manages these accounts (including the identity check required by law) and pays out to the organisation after the event; Pickeed collects the payments on the organisation's behalf, does not hold the money itself and triggers the payout on its behalf. Stripe receives the buyer's name and email address and the payment data or the organisation's details. Stripe is partly responsible for this itself and may process data in the USA (standard contractual clauses).

(Stripe Payments Europe Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) – identity verification for organisers of public events with tickets or a contribution: the ID document and selfie are captured and checked at Stripe; Pickeed only receives the result and the verified name. Stripe may process data in the USA (standard contractual clauses).
(Google Ireland Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) – only if set up: checks ticket and payment links against known fraud and malware sites. Google only receives the link address, no personal data.
(Open-Meteo.com) – weather forecasts and place search without an account. Only receives place names or rough coordinates, no information about people.

(United Kingdom) – map images for the Travel Guide. Our server fetches and caches them; OpenStreetMap only receives our server's address and the map section, no information about people. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
(Germany) – place search “Photon” for the “Where?” field. Only receives the search text via our server, no information about people.
(Germany) – routing service openrouteservice for “Walking route”. Only receives the start and destination points via our server, no information about people.

(USA) – GIF search in chats (only when you tap “GIF” or receive a GIF). Your device loads the search and GIFs directly from GIPHY; GIPHY receives the search term, IP address and device information, no information from your account.

, Cologne, Germany – automatic translation of published community ideas (title, description, tags). Only receives this text, no details about people. How long DeepL keeps the texts and whether it uses them to improve its service depends on DeepL’s terms for the DeepL API.
(Internet Security Research Group, USA) – issues the certificates for the encrypted connection. No data about you is transmitted.
(Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) – our email mailbox: messages to
and forwarded contact form messages are stored there. Microsoft may process data in the USA.

, Berlin, Germany – partner network for partner links (only if you open a partner link): Awin receives the destination address and Pickeed's click reference and, with the click itself, technical details such as your IP address and browser details, and may set cookies to attribute purchases or bookings. Awin and the partner are responsible for this themselves; Pickeed does not pass on any personal data to Awin.
Recipients in the USA: if a recipient is certified under the Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework, we rely on that; otherwise on standard contractual clauses with the adaptations required for Switzerland.
We do not sell data and do not pass it on for advertising purposes.

For operations and security there is a separate administration area with two-factor sign-in. Actions in this area are logged. The Pickeed team has no access to your chats and photos there. If someone reports a message, it only sees that one message with the author's name and the name of the plan – not the rest of the chat. If someone reports an image, it only sees the copy of that one image – no other photos. Otherwise it only sees what is needed to handle reports and for security.

As long as your account exists. If you delete your account, we immediately remove your email address, name and devices. Contributions to shared plans remain available to the group but appear as «Deleted account». Your own plans without other members are deleted too, as are provider and creator profiles with their offers, formats and statistics. We delete guest data without an account at the latest 12 months after the last activity or together with the plan. We keep check values of the age block for 30 days, notes on an age in texts until our team closes the case, at most 180 days, and messages from paused accounts to our team until the case is closed, at most 180 days and at the latest until the account is deleted. We keep encrypted database backups for 14 days; after that, all details are removed there as well.

All connections are encrypted (HTTPS). We store sign-in codes, sessions and invitations only as check values, and calendar addresses encrypted. Permissions are checked on the server with every access.

You can request information about your data, have it corrected or deleted, withdraw consent and – where applicable – object to processing or receive your data in a common format. In your profile you can download your data as a file and delete your account yourself at any time. For anything else, write to
. You can also lodge a complaint with the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) or, if you live in the EU, with your data protection authority.
If the way we process data changes, we will update this policy. We will inform you in Pickeed about significant changes.

/agb.title: Terms and Conditions – Pickeed
body: This is a translation. It fully reflects the German text. In case of contradictions, the German version applies; ambiguities that exist only in a translation are not held against you.

These terms apply to the use of Pickeed on pickeed.com and in the apps. Pickeed is free for private users, creators, companies and brands – including company spaces and public events (sections 6 and 7). Only the provider plan, for providers who want their offers recommended, is paid (section 7); it is consciously added on top, and no account ever becomes paid automatically. Payment is by card via Stripe on pickeed.com. As a launch offer, the provider plan is free until a set date; if you use it, you add a card for it (section 6a). For ticket sales via Pickeed checkout, the organisation bears the fees (section 7a). Features may continue to evolve.

Pickeed is a social media platform that gets you out with friends: people follow each other, discover events and plan together (discuss, suggest, vote and record). Pickeed is free for private plans. We strive for reliable operation but cannot promise uninterrupted availability. Maintenance and further development may occur.

To use Pickeed you need an account with a valid email address. Pickeed is for people aged 16 and over. When you sign up, you enter your correct date of birth. At 16 and 17 you have a normal account with special protection until 18 (see the privacy policy, «Protection until 18»). Only from 18 can you in particular: create open calls, create offers, have business profiles and public business or brand pages, show public company details, submit ideas, apply for verification, buy paid tickets, sell tickets and use other payment features, and use meetups and experiences. A creator page, applications to open calls and free tickets are available from 16. If there are doubts about your age, for example after reports, we may pause your account until your age is clear and delete it if you are under 16. False information about your age leads to the account being blocked or deleted. Keep access to your email account secure – anyone who can use it can sign in to Pickeed. You can delete your account yourself at any time. Exception: via an invitation link, you can take part as a guest without an account in a single private plan; these terms apply then too.

You are responsible for the content you enter in plans. In particular, unlawful, offensive, discriminatory or harassing content, spam, sharing other people's personal data without consent, and attempts to bypass security measures or access other people's plans are not allowed. We review reported violations. We may remove content and block accounts if these rules are broken.
You report content directly in Pickeed («Report» on messages, images, people, events, offers, provider and creator pages and open calls) or without an account via

. We handle reports of illegal content or risks to minors within 24 hours and all others within 24 hours too. We take child sexual abuse material offline immediately and report it to the police (fedpol). We inform you of decisions with reasons; you can object within 6 months via the

Pickeed has zero tolerance for objectionable content and for people who harass others. In particular, the following are not allowed: insults, threats, bullying and harassment; hate and incitement against people or groups (e.g. because of origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability); sexual or pornographic content; depictions of violence and calls for violence or self-harm; content that endangers minors; spam and fraud.

Consequences: we remove such content, as a rule within 24 hours of a report, and block accounts that break these rules – for serious breaches immediately and without warning. A word filter rejects serious insults when you send them. Creating and posting content requires an account and agreeing to these Terms and community rules. You can report any content and any person via «⋯» → «Report», block people and hide posts for yourself; contact:
You keep the rights to your content. You allow us to store it and display it to the members of the respective plan – solely to provide Pickeed.

If you recommend something for the Travel Guide by ticking «Also recommend to other travellers», you grant Pickeed a free, non-exclusive right, unlimited in time and place, to use the recommendation, edit it (e.g. shorten, correct, translate) and publish it in the Travel Guide without your name. For recommendations that have already been approved, this also applies after you delete your account; pending and rejected ones are deleted with the account.

If you share an idea with photos («Share an idea», «Share a creation»), you confirm that the photos are yours or that you may use them and that the people shown agree. You grant Pickeed a free, non-exclusive right, unlimited in place, to show the idea with its photos and source in Pickeed, on the public idea page and in link previews, and to adapt it for display (e.g. size, crop, alt text, tags), as long as it has not been withdrawn. The idea is public straight away; the Pickeed team reviews reported or suspicious ideas and can hide or remove them. Anyone who repeatedly breaks the rules can no longer share ideas.

If you upload a video with sound that is visible beyond your private circle (a post or memory for followers or public, “Event moments”, offers), choosing “My own music” or “I have the rights to the music” confirms that you may use the sound. We store this confirmation with the date and text version. If you don’t confirm anything, we publish the video without sound. We don’t ask in one-to-one chats or groups (members only).
Rights holders report infringements via “Report” (reason “Copyright”) or without an account via

. We hide a reported post until we’ve reviewed it. The person who uploaded it is informed and can submit a counter-notice; we decide with reasons and share the decision. After three confirmed violations we block uploads; every step is logged. Abusive reports can lead to the reporting account being blocked.

Songs from the search (favourite song, “Listening to …”, song stickers on posts) come from Apple’s catalogue (iTunes Search API). Pickeed only shows the title, artist, cover and a link to the song in Apple Music; the 30-second preview is only played directly from Apple after you tap (streamed), never stored, never automatically and never together with a photo or video. The preview only serves to discover the song on Apple – it is not background music for posts. Apple may require previews to be removed; Pickeed then switches them off immediately. Claims relating to the previews are directed to Pickeed, not Apple; Pickeed forwards them to Apple where necessary.
4c. Images and videos made with AI

When you post images or videos that were made or heavily edited with AI, you mark them with “Made or heavily edited with AI”. Pickeed then shows the label “AI”. If a file contains AI information (e.g. Content Credentials/C2PA or IPTC “DigitalSourceType”), we set the label automatically; you can’t remove it, but you can report it as wrongly detected. Pickeed labels its own AI images too.

Deceiving people with AI is not allowed: in particular realistic images, videos or voices of real people (deepfakes) without their consent, and content that fakes real events. Unlabelled AI content can be reported (reason “Unlabelled AI image”); moderation can add the label or remove the content and block the account for repeated violations.
Plans are private by default. Whoever makes a plan public or passes on invitations decides who can see or join it. Personal invitations can be revoked.

Companies and brands can use their own space with teams, templates and roles free of charge – no subscription and no price per person. A company space never becomes paid automatically. The organisers can cancel company subscriptions taken out earlier at any time on pickeed.com to the end of the paid month; until then the previous terms of these subscriptions apply. Whoever creates a company space confirms that they are authorised to act on behalf of the company. Section 6b (data processing on behalf of the company) applies to the data in the company space.

As a launch offer, the provider plan is free up to and including the date shown on pickeed.com (currently 31 May 2027, Zurich time). If you use it during this period, you take it out on pickeed.com via Stripe with a card (not in the apps). The card is only charged for the first time after that date, then monthly at the applicable price. Until then the subscription can be cancelled at any time, in which case nothing is charged. We send an email reminder 14 and 3 days before the first payment. This also applies to company and event subscriptions taken out earlier, as long as they have not been cancelled. Grandfathering: if you had already added a card for a subscription before this change (as of 3 November 2026), you keep the date promised then, 28 April 2028, as long as that subscription continues. If you added the card later but before the change to 31 May 2027, you likewise keep the date promised then, 30 September 2027.

Pickeed also does not charge the service fee on ticket sales through Pickeed checkout (section 7a) up to and including that date – for all organisations and in all currencies. For tickets sold after that, it is 2.5% of the ticket price plus 0.99 per ticket in CHF, EUR or USD, or 0.89 in GBP.

The provider benefits apply to all providers until that date, even without a subscription. After that date, the basic listing applies without a provider plan (section 7). Company spaces and «Tickets & contribution» are free regardless of that date. If Pickeed extends the free period, the first payment moves accordingly.
6b. Data processing on behalf of the company (company spaces)

The company is responsible for personal data in its company space (members, roles, teams, company plans and their content, attendance, feedback, budget approvals and annual planning). Pickeed processes this data as a processor on the company's behalf (Art. 9 FADP and, where applicable, Art. 28 GDPR) – only to provide the company space, according to the company's settings and instructions and not for its own purposes. Whoever creates a company space accepts this agreement on behalf of the company; Pickeed stores the acceptance with time and version.

Pickeed obliges everyone with access to confidentiality, protects the data with appropriate technical and organisational measures (encrypted connections, permission checks on every access, two-factor sign-in and logging in the admin area, encrypted backups) and only uses the sub-processors named in the privacy policy (section 5), currently Infomaniak (server), Supabase (database), Brevo (email delivery), Stripe (payments), Microsoft 365 (mailbox for support requests) and Apple and Google (notifications). Pickeed announces new sub-processors in Pickeed at least 30 days in advance; the company may object for good cause and end the company space.

Pickeed supports the company with requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, data export), notifies it of data security breaches without delay (Art. 24 FADP) and provides information on the measures taken on request. When the company space ends, the company can export the data beforehand; Pickeed then deletes it, and backups after 14 days, unless there is a statutory retention obligation. The company uses attendance, feedback and certificates of attendance only to organise its events, not to monitor performance or behaviour (Art. 328b CO, Art. 26 ArGV 3). On request, the company receives this agreement as a separate document (

Providers can list offers that are shown to groups matching their plan. Private individuals aged 18 and over can also create offers from their profile; the same rules as for providers apply. You are responsible yourself for whether you may offer your offer and which obligations (for example taxes or permits) come with it. Offers are visible as soon as they are published; Pickeed reviews them afterwards and may hide or block offers that violate these terms or applicable law without prior notice. Offers with suspicious links are reviewed by Pickeed before publication. Contracts for offers are concluded directly between the group and the provider; booking and payment do not take place in Pickeed. Pickeed is not a party to the contract and is not liable for providers' services. Providers are responsible for the accuracy of their details and the rights to their images.

In private plans, members settle costs among themselves (e.g. with «Split costs»); Pickeed does not accept any money. Public events sell tickets only through Pickeed checkout (section 7a) or link to a known ticket shop with its own buyer protection (e.g. Eventfrog, Ticketcorner, Eventbrite). Private payment methods such as an IBAN, TWINT number or PayPal link are not allowed for public events; ones entered earlier are no longer shown. Anyone who opens a private celebration to guests from the community describes the programme and rules honestly and may turn guests down.

Anyone who publishes a public event with a ticket price, contribution, payment options or ticket link provides true and complete information, names only themselves or expressly authorised payees and verifies their identity on request. Pickeed reviews the first such event and conspicuous changes before they appear publicly (with a confirmed Stripe account only suspicious links or texts, see section 7a); there is no entitlement to approval. The organisers alone are responsible for the service, cancellation and refunds. In case of suspected fraud or after reports, Pickeed may hide or remove events, payment details and ticket links and block accounts. Upon a lawful request, we disclose existing information (e.g. account, verified name, payment details, log) to law enforcement or other competent authorities.

«Tickets & contribution» (guests from the community, culture, contribution and payment options) is free for public events; no subscription is needed. For ticket sales via Pickeed checkout, only the service fee under section 7a applies. Event subscriptions taken out earlier continue under their previous terms until cancelled: the organisers can cancel them at any time on pickeed.com to the end of the paid month; they end automatically after the stated last day of the event, and immediately if the event is deleted or made private again. Pickeed is not registered for VAT; invoices are issued without VAT.

Providers can additionally take out a provider plan at CHF 9.90 (or EUR 9.90 or USD 9.90) per month per business profile as a conscious choice – a creator, company or brand account never becomes paid automatically; the basic listing with a business profile and up to 3 visible offers stays free. With an active provider plan, up to 20 offers are visible, the offers are highlighted as «Partner» in Picks (once the provider plan is paid, with the note «Partner · paid placement») and shown first among the results, and they can appear as «Sponsored» in the suggestions for a plan. The following applies: at most one sponsored offer per list, always labelled, only if the offer matches the plan's details (occasion, place, group size, budget, dietary needs), never ahead of the best-matching offer and never based on chat messages or personal profile details. There is no entitlement to a particular placement, number of impressions or enquiries. The provider takes out the subscription on pickeed.com by card via Stripe (not in the apps). It runs monthly, renews automatically and can be cancelled at any time to the end of the paid month. Without an active provider plan, the 3 most recently published offers stay visible; others are hidden but not deleted. As a launch offer, the provider plan benefits are free for all providers until the end of the free period (section 6a); there are no sponsored placements during this period. If you subscribe earlier, you only pay after that date. Pickeed is not registered for VAT; invoices are issued without VAT.

Pickeed is a platform. The seller of the tickets and the event organiser is the organisation of the event; the contract for taking part is concluded between the guest and the organisation. To sell tickets, the organisation opens a Stripe account (Stripe Connect) via Pickeed, confirms its identity and bank account there and accepts Stripe's terms for connected accounts (Stripe Connected Account Agreement). Pickeed collects the ticket prices on behalf and in the name of the organisation via Stripe (collection and payment processing); the payment service provider is Stripe. The payment goes directly to the organisation's Stripe account; Pickeed does not accept any money for its own account and does not operate any trust or escrow accounts. The organisation instructs Pickeed to trigger the payout from its Stripe account to its bank account after the event and to recover amounts for refunds to the organisation's guests and for fees via Stripe.

Guests pay in the event's currency, which depends on the country of the organisation's Stripe account (Swiss francs, euros, US dollars or pounds sterling): by card (including Apple Pay or Google Pay) and, for Swiss francs, also with TWINT, at most CHF 5000, EUR 5000, USD 5000 or GBP 4500 per payment. Pickeed does not convert currencies; any conversion fees charged by the guest's bank or card issuer are borne by the guest. Seats are reserved for up to 30 minutes while paying. Sales start no earlier than 80 days before the event and require a fixed date. After buying, the guest gets a ticket with QR code in Pickeed, a confirmation from Pickeed and a receipt from Stripe, and becomes a member of the plan (group chat).

The organisation instructs Pickeed to trigger the payout only after the event, usually 3 days after the end of the event; until then the money stays in its Stripe account. This payout hold serves as risk control for refunds, chargebacks and misuse; it does not create a trust relationship or a payment guarantee by Pickeed towards guests. If guests report within 48 hours after the end that the event did not take place, or if a payment is disputed, Pickeed reviews before the payout and may refund the guests on the organisation's behalf. If misuse is suspected, Pickeed may hold payouts, at most as long as Stripe allows (90 days).

If the organisation or Pickeed cancels an event, all guests automatically get the full ticket price back. Whether guests can otherwise return a ticket is set by the organisation (no returns, or returns up to 7 days or up to 48 hours before the event); the rule is shown on the event page before buying. Tickets that have been used cannot be returned. Depending on the bank or TWINT, the credit takes a few days.

The service fee is a fee paid by the organisation to Pickeed for providing ticket sales. It is shown to the organisation in Pickeed before selling (currently 2.5% of the ticket price plus 0.99 per ticket sold in CHF, EUR or USD, or 0.89 in GBP, always in the event's currency); during the introductory period, up to the date shown in Pickeed, Pickeed charges no service fee. For each event, the organisation decides whether it passes the service fee on to guests – it is then part of the price the organisation charges its guests, and Pickeed shows the ticket price, service fee and total before buying – or whether it bears the fee itself; it is then deducted from the ticket price. Stripe collects the service fee for Pickeed with the payment; Pickeed refunds it along with any refund. Stripe's fees are borne by the organisation; they are deducted at payout, also for tickets refunded later (Stripe does not refund its fee). All prices include any applicable VAT.

The organisation holds the event as described, is responsible for the service, permits and any taxes, and supports Pickeed with evidence in case of disputed payments (chargebacks). Pickeed is not the event organiser and is not liable to guests for the event taking place; mandatory statutory claims remain reserved.
Recovery of amounts for refunds and chargebacks

For refunds and disputed payments (chargebacks) relating to tickets for its event, the organisation bears the amounts and Stripe's fees towards Pickeed. Pickeed may (a) recover these amounts via Stripe from its Stripe account, also before a payout, (b) offset them against future payouts and (c) invoice any remainder, payable within 30 days. If a chargeback is lost because the event did not take place as described or the organisation's details were incorrect, the organisation also bears Stripe's dispute fee. For chargebacks due to card misuse by third parties for which the organisation is not responsible, Pickeed bears the dispute fee. The organisation confirms this paragraph with a separate tick box when setting up ticket sales; Pickeed stores the time and version.

Once the organisation's Stripe account is confirmed, events with tickets appear without prior review by Pickeed. Pickeed reviews suspicious links or texts before publication. Pickeed checks events afterwards and may hide them if they breach these terms or fraud is suspected; ticket sales then stop and all guests get their money back.

As a creator – a content creator or influencer, model, photographer, videographer, DJ, host, speaker, musician or artist – you can set up a creator profile with a public page at pickeed.com/@name – yourself and without approval, one per account, with at least one role. You can create a creator page from 16; at 16 and 17 the protection until 18 applies (no contact email, offers and payment features only from 18). As a content creator or influencer you need at least one social media profile of your own; for all other roles one link of your own is enough (website, for example a portfolio, or social media). The page is public straight away and can be found in search engines. Your formats (e.g. story, reel, shoot, DJ set, hosting or talk) appear like offers in Picks and for matching plans, companies see you as a suggestion for their events, and you can show your own public events as fan events («An event by @name»).

Pickeed does not broker and takes no commission. Agreements and payment are made directly between you and the company, group or person; Pickeed is not a party to the contract and is not liable for your services. You are responsible for the accuracy of your details – including your roles, reach, audience and languages, which Pickeed does not check –, for the rights to pictures and content (also towards the people shown), for the linked website and social media profiles being your own, and for clearly labelling paid collaborations and advertising in your posts as advertising in accordance with the Swiss Federal Act against Unfair Competition (UCA) and the rules of the respective platform.

The rules for providers in section 7 apply to creators accordingly: the page and formats are visible as soon as they are published, Pickeed reviews them afterwards and checks links as for providers, and creator pages can be reported. In case of violations of these terms or applicable law, Pickeed may hide formats and block the creator profile without prior notice; the page, formats and suggestions are then no longer visible, and a blocked profile can only be deleted via Pickeed. Otherwise you can delete your creator profile yourself at any time; the page, formats, picture and statistics are then deleted, and fan events remain as normal events.

With an open call you look for someone for your occasion (e.g. DJ, photography, hosting). You may create open calls from the age of 18; as a creator you can apply and write in the thread of an application from 16. Give truthful details about the occasion, date, place and budget, be respectful and don't use open calls for advertising, spam, recruiting for other purposes or collecting contact details.

Pickeed does not broker, takes no commission and is not a party to any contract. You agree arrangements, prices, payment, insurance and cancellations directly with each other; Pickeed checks neither services nor ability to pay and is not liable for them. You can report open calls, applications, messages and people and block people. Pickeed may hide open calls, applications and messages and block accounts if these rules are broken.
Pickeed is not an emergency service.

In an emergency, call the local emergency number (in Switzerland and Europe 112, police 117, ambulance 144). Trusted persons, check-ins, emergency info and the emergency numbers shown are aids without guarantee: notifications may arrive late or not at all (e.g. without a network or with notifications turned off), and numbers, travel advice and deadlines can change. Check them locally and with official sources.

Ideas, the Travel Guide and recommendations in Pickeed are suggestions without guarantee of accuracy, opening hours, prices, safety or availability. Check details locally and with the provider; Pickeed is not liable for third-party services.
7f. Usernames, company and brand pages, creator invitations

Creators, providers and companies can choose a username (pickeed.com/@name; 3–30 characters, unique, one shared namespace). Only choose a name that you or your company are entitled to. Not allowed are names that imitate other people, brands or organisations or could be confused with them, misleading, offensive or unlawful names, and registering names in advance to block them or sell them on (no trading in usernames). Certain names are reserved for Pickeed. In the event of breaches or justified claims by third parties (e.g. trademark or name rights), Pickeed may withdraw or change a username and assign it to someone else; we let you know beforehand unless the abuse is obvious. Once a profile or page has been deleted, its username may be assigned again later. There is no entitlement to a particular username.

Companies can switch on a public company or brand page. Only the «organisation» role can do this; by switching it on, you confirm that you may act on behalf of the company and that you are at least 18. The page only shows what the company releases for it (name, logo, username, category, short description, website, social media, public events and confirmed collaborations) – never employees, teams, internal plans, budgets or open calls. It is public and may appear in search engines; the company is responsible for the information. The rules for providers in section 7 apply accordingly: Pickeed reviews pages afterwards, pages can be reported, and Pickeed may hide a page in the event of breaches. The company can switch the page off at any time. Collaborations only appear if both the company and the creator agree, and either side can remove them at any time.

Only the Pickeed team awards the «Verified brand» badge, at the organisation's request and after a check (e.g. whether the applicant's email address matches the website's domain and whether the website or social media link back to the page); there is no entitlement to it. It only confirms that, according to this check, the page belongs to the brand named – not quality, an endorsement or a partnership with Pickeed. Pretending to be another person, company or brand breaches these terms. Pickeed may withdraw the badge at any time, in particular in the event of false information or imitation, if the name, website or owner changes, or after justified reports from third parties, and in such cases hide the page and block the account.

Creators can invite other creators to Pickeed with their personal invite link (pickeed.com/c/…). There is no money, reward, commission or ranking for this; the invite link is not a referral link within the meaning of section 8. Only invite people who want to join – no spam, no bought or fake profiles. You can renew the link at any time; the old one then stops working. In the event of abuse, Pickeed may block invite links. Only the Pickeed team awards «Founding creator» status; there is no entitlement to it.

Some links in Pickeed are partner links (advertising) and are always labelled «Partner link» – for example shop links on the wish list, «Get it online» in the list of what to bring, help with trips and outings, links in the Travel Guide and partner offers in Idea Pick and Discover. If you buy or book through such a link, Pickeed may receive a commission; the price does not change for you. Partner offers come from partner shops, not from Pickeed providers; they always appear after the real results and do not influence the order of other content. The contract is concluded solely between you and the partner; Pickeed is not a party to it and is not liable for the partners' offers, prices, availability or services. What is transmitted when you click is explained in the

With «Meet me», people (e.g. creators, musicians, athletes) offer meetups; with «Experiences», companies offer visits (e.g. open day, guided tour, workshop, taster day). The offering party is responsible for the offer and for carrying it out; the contract for the meetup is concluded between it and the booking person or company. Pickeed provides the platform and processes the payment on behalf of the offering party via Stripe (as in section 7a).

Meetups and experiences are only for people aged 18 and over. Before every offer and every booking, both sides confirm the «Rules for meetups»; we store the version and time. Only public places or real workplaces and venues (e.g. concert hall, set, stadium, studio) are allowed, for experiences the company’s verified location – never private addresses, hotels or flats. Sexual, escort and dating offers are prohibited. Until the meetup, contact and payment run only via Pickeed. Violations lead to removal of the offer and to a ban.

Anyone receiving money sets up a payout account with Stripe including an identity check. Up to and including 31.05.2027 (Zurich time) Pickeed charges no fee; after that, Pickeed keeps 10 % of the price as a fee. The time of booking is decisive. The offering party bears Stripe’s fees. The payout is made at the earliest three days after the meetup, provided nothing was reported. With a linked management, the payout goes to the person, to the management or is split – as confirmed by the person.

The booking person can cancel up to 48 hours before the start and gets the full amount back; after that, cancelling is possible without a refund. If the offering party cancels or the meetup does not take place, everyone gets the full amount back. «Booking verified» only means that the identity was checked at Stripe; Pickeed awards the «Verified» badge separately.

Verified companies can request people for performances, meet & greets or similar services. The person accepts or declines; the invoice contains the company’s details and VAT number. The offering party is itself responsible for taxes and charges on its income.

You can recommend Pickeed with your personal link from your profile. For every 100 active referrals you receive a one-off reward of CHF 50.– (residence in Switzerland or Liechtenstein) or EUR 50.– (other countries); with 200 active referrals, two rewards.

A referral is active when a person signs up as a new user via your link, has confirmed their email address and has been active in a plan on two different calendar days within 60 days of signing up (e.g. wrote a message, answered Time Pick, created or joined a plan). Only the first referral counts per new account. Your own, existing, deleted or suspended accounts don't count.

We pay the reward by bank transfer, after you have requested it in Pickeed with your name and IBAN and we have checked it – usually within 30 days. Apart from the cash payout during an event campaign (see below), there are no other payment methods and no offsetting. You are responsible for any taxes on the reward.

At fairs and events, Pickeed occasionally runs event campaigns. If you take part via the link or QR code at the Pickeed stand (or our team adds you), a new sign-up via your personal link during the campaign already counts as an active referral once the new person has created or joined a plan. Before the start and after the end of the campaign, the normal rules apply. Each referral counts only once, and campaign referrals count towards the 100 active referrals. Because many people on site use the same network, we check campaign referrals individually instead of automatically by address.

During an event campaign you take part in, and up to 24 hours after it ends, you can request a due reward in cash at the Pickeed stand instead of by bank transfer. The cash payout is made only in person and against a receipt (place, time, paying team member); afterwards you confirm receipt in Pickeed. As above, the currency depends on your place of residence. If you dispute receipt, we examine the case on the basis of the receipt.

If we suspect abuse during an event campaign – such as sign-ups without real use, duplicate accounts or pressure on visitors – we may not count campaign referrals, end your participation and refuse a cash payout.

In case of abuse – such as fake or duplicate accounts, automated sign-ups or misleading advertising – we may not count referrals, refuse or reclaim payouts and suspend accounts. We may change or end the programme for the future and will announce this in Pickeed at least 30 days in advance. Full sets of 100 active referrals reached by then will be paid out if you request them within 60 days afterwards.

body: Best time to go: March–May, October–November
– Thousands of red torii gates up the mountain – almost empty early in the morning.
– The Golden Pavilion reflected in its pond.
– A path between towering bamboo stalks in the west of the city.
– A wooden temple on the hillside with views over the city.
– The old quarter of tea houses – please don't photograph geishas.
– A canal-side walk lined with cherry trees.
– «Kyoto's kitchen»: pickles, tofu and matcha sweets.
– The refined seasonal multi-course cuisine of Kyoto.
– Matcha the traditional way, often with a short introduction.
– A narrow riverside alley lined with small restaurants.
– The Great Buddha at Todai-ji and tame deer in the park.
– Street food in Dotonbori and the castle, a short train ride away.
– The white castle, one of Japan's finest.
Buses and two metro lines, plus bikes; by train from Kansai Airport and by Shinkansen from Tokyo.

/travel-guide/osaka.title: Travel Guide Osaka, Japan – Pickeed
/travel-guide/osaka.description: Osaka (Japan): Osaka Castle, Dotonbori and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go March–May, October–November – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: March–May, October–November
– The city's landmark, with a museum, moats and a large park – especially lovely at cherry blossom time.
– A canal lined with neon signs, a giant crab and the famous Glico running man – liveliest at night.
– A nostalgic district around an observation tower, full of kushikatsu bars.
– Two towers linked at the top by an open-air observation deck – ideal at sunset.
– One of Japan's oldest Buddhist temples, founded in the 6th century.
– A theme park with film worlds and Super Nintendo World – go early.
– Batter balls filled with octopus, fresh from the stall – Osaka's street food par excellence.
– A savoury pancake with cabbage, cooked on a hotplate at your table.
– A covered market street with seafood, fruit and small bites.
– Deep-fried skewers – dip in the shared sauce only once, that's the rule.
– Tame deer in the park and the giant Buddha of Todai-ji.
– The white castle is a UNESCO site and one of Japan's finest – close by Shinkansen.
– A port city backed by mountains, famous for its beef.
– A sacred mountain of monasteries – spend a night in a temple with vegetarian monks' cuisine.
Metro and JR trains with an IC card (ICOCA or Suica); trains run from Kansai Airport into town, and Kyoto and Nara are under an hour away.
Plug type A/B, 100 V – pack an adapter for Swiss plugs.

/travel-guide/siem-reap.title: Travel Guide Siem Reap, Cambodia – Pickeed
/travel-guide/siem-reap.description: Siem Reap (Cambodia): Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom and Bayon and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–February – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – The world's largest temple – at sunrise its towers are reflected in the pond.
– A royal city with the Bayon and its hundreds of smiling stone faces.
– A temple embraced by strangler figs and giant tree roots.
– A small pink sandstone temple with exquisite carvings.
– A good introduction to the history of the Khmer Empire.
– Psar Chas, with spices, silk and souvenirs.
– Coconut curry steamed in a banana leaf – Cambodia's best-known dish.
– Stir-fried beef with a pepper and lime dip.
– Bars, foot massages and street food – the party strip at night.
– Meat and vegetables on a domed grill plate with broth.
– Stilt and floating villages on Southeast Asia's largest lake.
– A sacred mountain with a waterfall and lingas carved into the riverbed.
– An overgrown jungle temple, less visited than Angkor.
Reach the temples by tuk-tuk, with a driver or by bike; you need a temple pass for Angkor. Alongside the riel, US dollars are widely used.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/luang-prabang.title: Travel Guide Luang Prabang, Laos – Pickeed
/travel-guide/luang-prabang.description: Luang Prabang (Laos): Old Town, Wat Xieng Thong and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–February – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – Temples and colonial houses on a peninsula between the Mekong and Nam Khan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– The town's most magnificent temple, with sweeping low roofs.
– Monks walk the streets at dawn – watch quietly from a distance and without flash.
– Steps up the hill in the middle of town – popular at sunset.
– The former royal residence, home to the revered Pha Bang Buddha.
– Textiles and crafts from the hill peoples, calm and unhurried.
– Sticky rice eaten with your fingers, with a spicy minced-meat salad and herbs.
– Crispy Mekong river weed with sesame – a local snack.
– Buffet stalls and grilled fish at small prices.
– A Beerlao at a riverside bar.
– Turquoise pools for swimming and a bear rescue centre.
– A Mekong boat trip to caves filled with Buddha statues.
– Two days on the river towards the Thai border – a backpacker classic.
A small airport and a station on the fast railway to Vientiane; the old town is compact and easy on foot or by bike.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/kuala-lumpur.title: Travel Guide Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia – Pickeed
/travel-guide/kuala-lumpur.description: Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia): Petronas Towers and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go January–February, June–August – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: January–February, June–August
– The twin towers with their skybridge – in the evening, fountains in KLCC Park.
– A Hindu shrine in limestone caves above a colourful staircase, guarded by a golden statue.
– Where independence was declared in 1957, surrounded by colonial buildings.
– One of Southeast Asia's largest collections of Islamic art.
– Market, temples and street art, right by the Sri Mahamariamman Temple.
– A telecom tower on a forested hill in the middle of the city.
– The street food lane in Bukit Bintang, full of tables at night.
– Coconut rice with sambal, peanuts and anchovies – the national dish.
– Flatbread with curry at Indian-Muslim eateries, often open round the clock.
– A historic port with Portuguese, Dutch and Peranakan heritage, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Tea plantations and cool air in the highlands.
– The administrative capital with a pink mosque and lakeside bridges.
The KLIA Ekspres runs from the airport to the centre; in town use LRT, MRT and monorail, plus Grab. Cover shoulders and knees for mosques.

/travel-guide/langkawi.title: Travel Guide Langkawi, Malaysia – Pickeed
/travel-guide/langkawi.description: Langkawi (Malaysia): SkyBridge and cable car and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–April – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A steep cable car up Gunung Mat Cincang and a curved suspension bridge.
– A boat trip through mangroves and karst, with sea eagles.
– A lively beach with bars and sunsets.
– A quiet beach with casuarina trees and views of rocky islets.
– A waterfall with natural pools in the rainforest.
– A giant eagle statue at the harbour, the island's namesake.
– The pasar malam moves to a different spot on the island each evening.
– Grilled fish and chilli crab by the water.
– Rice with your choice from a buffet – cheap and typical.
– A duty-free island: drinks in the sand at sunset.
– By boat to the freshwater lake on Pulau Dayang Bunting.
– A marine park for snorkelling with corals and reef sharks.
– Paddle quietly through channels and caves.
Fly or take the ferry to the island; a hire car or Grab is best there, as buses are scarce.
Plug type G, 240 V – pack an adapter for Swiss plugs.

/travel-guide/penang.title: Travel Guide Penang, Malaysia – Pickeed
/travel-guide/penang.description: Penang (Malaysia): George Town old town, Street art and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go December–March – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – Shophouses, temples and mosques – a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Murals and wrought-iron figures tell the town's story along the lanes.
– Stilt villages of Chinese clans built over the water.
– An ornate clan house with rich carvings.
– One of Southeast Asia's largest Buddhist temples, on the hillside above Air Itam.
– Up by funicular for cooler air and views.
– Penang is considered Malaysia's street food capital – try Gurney Drive.
– Smoky stir-fried rice noodles with prawns and cockles.
– A sour fish noodle soup with tamarind – Penang's classic.
– Banana-leaf curries, sweets and teh tarik.
– Jungle trails to quiet coves such as Monkey Beach.
– A beach and night market on the island's north coast.
– Limestone hills, cave temples and famous white coffee on the mainland.
An airport on the island, plus bridges and a ferry to the mainland; in George Town go on foot, by trishaw, bus or Grab.
Plug type G, 240 V – pack an adapter for Swiss plugs.

/travel-guide/kathmandu.title: Travel Guide Kathmandu, Nepal – Pickeed
/travel-guide/kathmandu.description: Kathmandu (Nepal): Durbar Square, Swayambhunath and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go March–April, October–November – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: March–April, October–November
– The royal palace and temples of Newar culture, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– The «Monkey Temple» on a hilltop, with the eyes of the Buddha.
– One of the world's largest stupas, circled clockwise by pilgrims.
– A sacred Hindu temple by the river with cremation ghats – observe respectfully.
– The neighbouring city with one of the finest Durbar squares and crafts.
– A tranquil neoclassical garden amid the bustle.
– Steamed dumplings with a spicy tomato dip.
– Lentils with rice and vegetables – refills are on the house.
– Bara (lentil patties) and choila, spiced grilled meat.
– Masala tea looking out over the city's rooftops.
– A medieval royal city with a potters' square and pagodas.
– Sunrise over the Himalayan range on a clear day.
– A lakeside town facing 8,000-metre peaks, the start of many treks.
– Lowland jungle with rhinos and, with luck, tigers.
Taxis and ride-hailing apps, on foot in the old town; to Pokhara by bus or domestic flight. Treks require permits, often arranged through an agency.

/travel-guide/palawan.title: Travel Guide Palawan, Philippines – Pickeed
/travel-guide/palawan.description: Palawan (Philippines): Bacuit Bay, El Nido, Coron and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go December–May – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – Limestone cliffs, lagoons and beaches – island to island by boat.
– Wreck diving on Japanese WWII ships and Kayangan Lake.
– A boat ride into a cave of stalactites – a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– A long stretch of sand north of El Nido.
– A relaxed fishing village without big hotels.
– Islets and sandbars off Puerto Princesa.
– Raw fish in vinegar and lime – the Filipino ceviche.
– Meat braised in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic.
– Shaved ice with fruit, beans and coconut milk – all mixed together.
– Lunch of grilled fish and fruit right on the beach.
– The classic tours A to D to lagoons and hidden beaches.
– Between El Nido and Coron, camping on islands overnight.
– A safari park with giraffes and zebras on an island near Coron.
Fly from Manila to Puerto Princesa, El Nido or Coron (Busuanga), with vans and ferries in between. Many beaches are reachable only by boat.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.
Plug type A/B/C, 220 V – pack an adapter for Swiss plugs.

/travel-guide/sri-lanka.title: Travel Guide Sri Lanka – Pickeed
/travel-guide/sri-lanka.description: Sri Lanka (Sri Lanka): Sigiriya, Temple of the Tooth, Kandy and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go December–April – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A fortress atop a rock monolith with frescoes and a lion gate.
– The country's most important Buddhist shrine, beside Kandy Lake.
– The Dutch-built fortified old town by the sea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Five caves full of Buddha statues and murals.
– Ruins of a medieval royal city, best explored by bike.
– A stone viaduct surrounded by tea plantations.
– A seafront promenade in Colombo, with street food and kites in the evening.
– Rice with lots of small curries of vegetables, lentils and fish.
– Bowl-shaped rice-flour pancakes, often with an egg.
– Chopped flatbread with vegetables, noisily chopped on the griddle.
– Fresh in the highlands, for example at a tea factory near Nuwara Eliya.
– One of the world's most beautiful train rides through tea hills.
– A jeep safari with a chance of leopards and elephants.
– Blue whales and dolphins off the south coast, in season.
– A night-time pilgrim climb to sunrise on the sacred summit.
Slow but beautiful train routes, plus tuk-tuks; many travellers hire a private driver. The monsoons hit the south-west and the east at different times.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/busan.title: Travel Guide Busan, South Korea – Pickeed
/travel-guide/busan.description: Busan (South Korea): Haeundae Beach and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go May–June, September–October – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: May–June, September–October
– Korea's best-known city beach, with high-rises and a promenade.
– Colourful houses on a hillside, winding lanes and art on every corner.
– A Buddhist temple set right on the seaside rocks.
– Korea's largest fish market – upstairs they cook what you buy.
– A beach facing the suspension bridge, lit up at night.
– A large mountain temple in the forest on the edge of the city.
– Pork and rice soup – Busan's classic dish.
– Cold wheat noodles in a tangy broth, perfect in summer.
– Sweet pancakes filled with seeds and syrup, near BIFF Square.
– Hoe – raw fish with gochujang sauce and soju.
– The old capital of the Silla kingdom, with burial mounds and Bulguksa Temple.
– One of Korea's most beautiful cherry blossom spots in spring.
– Sea cliffs with a lighthouse at the city's southern tip.
By KTX high-speed train from Seoul; metro and buses in the city with a T-money card.

/travel-guide/seoul.title: Travel Guide Seoul, South Korea – Pickeed
/travel-guide/seoul.description: Seoul (South Korea): Gyeongbokgung Palace and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go April–May, September–October – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: April–May, September–October
– The largest Joseon-era royal palace, with a changing of the guard at the main gate.
– Lanes of traditional wooden houses between two palaces – keep it quiet, people live here.
– On Namsan hill with views over the whole city – best in the evening.
– A UNESCO World Heritage Site; the garden can only be visited on a guided tour.
– Tea houses, galleries and crafts in a pedestrian quarter.
– Zaha Hadid's curving building, lit up at night, surrounded by late-night fashion markets.
– A restored stream right through downtown – perfect for an evening stroll.
– The city's oldest market: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mini gimbap.
– Grill samgyeopsal at the table with banchan and lettuce wraps.
– Evening stalls with tteokbokki, skewers and egg bread.
– A student district with buskers, cafés and clubs until late.
– Fried chicken with beer – a Korean evening ritual.
– A guided trip to the border with North Korea – only on a tour, with your passport.
– An 18th-century city wall, reachable by metro.
– Tree-lined avenues on a river island, especially lovely in autumn.
– Granite peaks and temples on the city's edge – pack hiking boots.
A dense metro network paid with a rechargeable T-money card; the AREX train links Incheon Airport with the city.
Plug type C/F, 220 V – pack an adapter for Swiss plugs.

/travel-guide/bangkok.title: Travel Guide Bangkok, Thailand – Pickeed
/travel-guide/bangkok.description: Bangkok (Thailand): Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew, Wat Pho and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–February – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
– The Emerald Buddha in the palace grounds – cover shoulders and knees.
– The huge reclining Buddha and a famous massage school.
– The Temple of Dawn on the river, beautiful at sunset.
– Thousands of stalls – from clothes to plants.
– Ride the express boat past temples and towers.
– A teak house with silk art and a tropical garden.
– Chinatown at night: noodles, seafood and desserts.
– Fried noodles and spicy papaya salad – classics on every corner.
– The skyline from above, best at sunset.
– Sticky rice with coconut milk and ripe mango.
– Temple ruins of the old royal capital, explored by train or bike.
– Vendors sell from boats – go early.
– A market right on the tracks that folds away when the train comes.
Skytrain (BTS), metro (MRT) and boats on the Chao Phraya; the Airport Rail Link serves Suvarnabhumi.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/chiang-mai.title: Travel Guide Chiang Mai, Thailand – Pickeed
/travel-guide/chiang-mai.description: Chiang Mai (Thailand): Doi Suthep, Wat Chedi Luang and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–February – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A golden temple on the local mountain, reached by a naga staircase.
– A massive, partly ruined chedi in the heart of the old city.
– The city's most important temple, in Lanna style.
– A square old city with remains of walls and gates such as Tha Phae Gate.
– The whole old city turns into a market for crafts and street food.
– A trendy area with cafés, galleries and co-working spaces.
– Curry noodle soup topped with crispy noodles – Northern Thailand's classic.
– A spicy herb sausage from the north, fresh off the grill.
– Pound curry paste on a farm and cook your own dishes.
– An evening market with food stalls and live music.
– Thailand's highest mountain, with pagodas, waterfalls and cool air.
– Choose one without riding or shows – observe rather than use.
– The White Temple, Wat Rong Khun, and the Blue Temple.
– A laid-back mountain town reached by a winding road.
Red shared taxis (songthaew), tuk-tuks and Grab; the old city inside the moat is easy on foot.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/koh-samui.title: Travel Guide Koh Samui, Thailand – Pickeed
/travel-guide/koh-samui.description: Koh Samui (Thailand): Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai), Chaweng and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go February–August – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A golden Buddha statue on a small island, reached by a causeway.
– The island's longest and liveliest beach.
– A quieter beach with the well-known Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks.
– Wooden houses, boutiques and a street market on Fridays.
– Two waterfalls inland with pools for swimming.
– A colourful temple with a many-armed Guanyin statue by a lake.
– Dinner with your feet in the sand.
– Skewers, pad thai and fresh fruit shakes.
– Learn to cook Thai classics yourself.
– A sundowner looking out to the neighbouring islands.
– Over 40 islands with kayaking, a lagoon and a viewpoint.
– Known for the Full Moon Party, otherwise quiet bays.
– A small island and one of the most popular places to learn to dive.
Fly to the island or take the ferry from the mainland; on the island, taxis, shared pick-ups and hire cars. The rainy season here is mainly October to December.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/krabi.title: Travel Guide Krabi, Thailand – Pickeed
/travel-guide/krabi.description: Krabi (Thailand): Railay, Phra Nang Beach, Ao Nang and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–April – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A peninsula of limestone cliffs, reachable only by boat – a climbers' paradise.
– A dream beach with a cave and rocks rising from the sea.
– A beach town and the starting point for boat trips.
– Well over a thousand steps to a Buddha with panoramic views.
– A natural emerald-green pool in the forest.
– A small riverside town with a night market and mangroves.
– Southern Thai curries, roti and desserts.
– Fresh from the grill on Ao Nang beach.
– A paper-thin pancake with banana and condensed milk.
– A shake on the beach as the sun sets behind the rocks.
– By longtail to Koh Poda, Chicken Island and a sandbar.
– Long, quiet beaches – ideal for families.
– A lagoon enclosed by cliffs, to explore by kayak.
Krabi Airport, then a taxi or bus to Ao Nang; longtail boats to the beaches and islands.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/phuket.description: Phuket (Thailand): Phuket Town, Big Buddha, Wat Chalong and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go November–April – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – An old town of pastel-coloured Sino-Portuguese shophouses.
– A white marble statue on a hilltop with views across the island.
– The busiest beach and the island's party strip.
– The island's southern tip, popular at sunset.
– Grilled fish and prawns, often picked fresh.
– Fried yellow noodles, a legacy of Chinese immigrants.
– The Lard Yai market with street food and music on Thalang Road.
– A mild curry with peanuts and potatoes, typical of the south.
– Limestone cliffs, turquoise water and the famous Maya Bay.
– Kayaking among karst islands, plus «James Bond Island».
– One of Thailand's best diving areas, open only in the dry season.
Taxis and Grab; a hire scooter is only worthwhile if you're experienced and wear a helmet; island trips by boat.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/hanoi.title: Travel Guide Hanoi, Vietnam – Pickeed
/travel-guide/hanoi.description: Hanoi (Vietnam): Old Quarter, Hoan Kiem Lake and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go March–April, October–November – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: Best time to go: March–April, October–November
– 36 streets, each once devoted to a single trade.
– The lake with the red bridge, pedestrianised at weekends.
– Vietnam's first university, set around quiet courtyards.
– A monumental building on Ba Dinh Square – mind the dress code.
– Houses so close to the tracks the train almost brushes the doors.
– An ancient art: puppets dancing on water.
– Noodle soup for breakfast, the way Hanoi invented it.
– Grilled pork with rice noodles and herbs.
– Coffee topped with whipped egg yolk – sweet as dessert.
– Fresh draught beer on tiny plastic stools at street corners.
– Limestone karsts in the sea – best with a night on board.
– «Ha Long on land»: boat rides through caves and rice fields.
– A mountain town with rice terraces in the north, by night train or bus.
Walk in the Old Quarter, otherwise use taxi or motorbike apps; cross the street slowly and steadily.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/hoi-an.title: Travel Guide Hoi An, Vietnam – Pickeed
/travel-guide/hoi-an.description: Hoi An (Vietnam): Old Town, Japanese Covered Bridge and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go February–May – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A well-preserved trading port with yellow houses, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Silk lanterns glow everywhere at night, and paper lights float on the Thu Bon river.
– Ornate halls of the Chinese merchant communities, such as the Fujian hall.
– Made-to-measure clothes within days – order early in your stay.
– A relaxed beach, reachable by bike through rice fields.
– Thick noodles with pork and herbs – found only here.
– Hoi An is considered one of the best towns for the baguette sandwich.
– Delicate rice-paper dumplings with shrimp, shaped like roses.
– With a market visit and a boat ride to a countryside cooking school.
– Ruined Cham temples in the jungle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Limestone hills with caves and pagodas between Hoi An and Da Nang.
– A scenic road over the coastal mountains – popular by motorbike.
The nearest airport is Da Nang, about 30 km away; explore the old town on foot or by bike.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

/travel-guide/fribourg.description: Fribourg (Switzerland): St Nicholas Cathedral and more. Food and nightlife, day trips, best time to go May–October – in the Pickeed Travel Guide.
body: – A Gothic tower with wide views and Art Nouveau stained glass.
– One of Switzerland's largest medieval old towns, high above the river.
– A covered wooden bridge in the lower Auge district.
Espace Jean Tinguely – Niki de Saint Phalle
– Moving machines and colourful sculptures in an old tram depot.
– The Sarine divides German and French – street signs in both languages.
– A wild, romantic walk just below the town.
– An autumn feast with cuchaule bread and Bénichon mustard.
– With the famous double cream from the Gruyère region.
– A student town with lively bars.
– A medieval little town with a castle and a show dairy.
– A town wall and lakeshore, half an hour away.
– A mountain lake in the Fribourg Prealps, with cross-country skiing in winter.
The old town is steep – the funicular runs with waste water as counterweight; otherwise TPF buses.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

Old town and St Pierre Cathedral
– From the towers, views over the lake and the Jura.
– A public lido on the lake, with sauna and fondue in winter.
– The UN's Geneva headquarters, with guided tours.
– Monumental figures in Parc des Bastions.
– Exhibitions at the world's largest particle physics lab.
– An Italian-style quarter full of bistros.
– Perch fillets from the lake, with fries.
– Cosy restaurants around Place du Bourg-de-Four.
– Cable car up the local mountain in France.
– A medieval lakeside village, reached by boat.
– Canals and a turquoise lake in Savoy.
Trams, buses and the yellow Mouettes boats across the lake; the airport is minutes away by train.
Service is usually included – rounding up is a nice gesture.

– A dying lion carved in rock, in memory of the Swiss Guards.
– A city wall with towers and views over the roofs.
– Trains, planes and boats to explore.
– A lakeside concert hall with a sweeping roof.
– By paddle steamer to Weggis, Vitznau or Flüelen.
– A puff pastry pie with veal – Lucerne's speciality.
– Coffee and cake with views of Pilatus and Rigi.
– Rösti and fondue in old guild houses.
– Up on the world's steepest cogwheel railway, down by cable car.
– The «Queen of the Mountains» with views over many lakes.
– A cable car with an open upper deck (CabriO).
The old town on foot; boats on Lake Lucerne and mountain railways in every direction.

– A medieval street lined with arcades.
– Swimming, walking and boating on Lake Murten.
– A Savoyard castle at the edge of the old town.
– The story of the Battle of Murten in 1476.
– A vine-covered hill between Lakes Murten and Neuchâtel.
– A yeast cake topped with cream and sugar.
– Chasselas and red wines from Mont Vully.
– In the restaurants by the harbour.
– The Roman amphitheatre of the former capital Aventicum.
– Across Lakes Murten, Neuchâtel and Biel.
– A tropical dome full of butterflies in Kerzers.
The little town on foot; boats across Lake Murten and through the canals to Neuchâtel and Biel.

body: – On the hill above the old town, with views over the lake.
– Houses of the typical yellow Jura limestone and fine fountains.
– The Jaquet-Droz automata write, draw and play music.
– An archaeology park on the lake – the Celts of La Tène.
– A stroll and a swim with views of the Alps.
– The writer's works and home high above the town.
– Chasselas, Œil-de-Perdrix rosé and the cloudy «non filtré» in winter.
– Cheese fondue made with local white wine.
– The «green fairy» comes from the nearby Val-de-Travers.
– Perch fillets and whitefish in the lakeside restaurants.
– A natural rock amphitheatre in the Jura, often with ibex on the rim.
– Watchmaking towns laid out in a grid – a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
– Absinthe distilleries and the Areuse gorge.

– Castle ruins on the neighbouring hill overlooking the Rhône valley.
– The cathedral, town hall and lanes with wine bars.
– One of Europe's largest underground lakes, explored by boat.
– A small lake among vineyards on the edge of town.
– Walks along old irrigation channels, such as the Bisse du Torrent-Neuf.
– Best with Raclette du Valais AOP.
– Taste Valais wines straight from the winemaker.
– Fresh in summer, otherwise as Abricotine brandy.
– Air-dried meat, bacon, cheese and rye bread.
– The world's tallest gravity dam, in the Val d'Hérémence.
– Boulders perched on earth pillars in the Val d'Hérens.
– A sunny plateau with lakes, golf and skiing.

– See the city from the water.

– Cycle along the canal to a little town.
– Take the coast tram from resort to resort.
– A lively university town, half an hour away.

– A historic amusement park in the city centre.
– A bronze statue from Andersen's tale on the waterfront.
